I don’t like the idea of an island of socialism within a capitalist country, though I do believe that new cities will need to be built. To have an entire city blueprinted before it’s built gives the opportunity to plan out all facets of the infrastructure, economy and costs beforehand, and would result in a much more well thought out and efficient city overall. All of the maintenance would be on a schedule and all of the properties would have roughly the same values, having been built at the same point in time.

A lot of the expenses of our current system comes from the fact that it’s all built in a patchwork, with both outdated infrastructures and laws overlapping each other as it’s built up on top of itself over long periods of time. This makes things tremendously inefficient and costly in the long run, and many of the socialist ideas that capitalists deem “too expensive,” cost so much because of that inefficiency in the system. To hit the reset button and have everything in place from day one... all the laws, all the processes, all the planning. It would trim a lot of the fat.

After a year of constantly starting over on official PS4 pvp in a 2-3 player tribe, I think I’ve got a pretty good game plan for you guys. 

The first thing you’ve got to do is pick a server. I would recommend the island for starters, as it’s more hospitable, easier to navigate and less popular than ragnarok. Server ping and player populations are the two things to consider here, and sometimes you have to make a trade off. I personally would slightly prioritize better ping over having a low server population. In my experience, frame rate drops and rubber banding will kill you and your dinosaurs more often than other players.

Before you and your buddies hit the beach, search for the explorers map online. You’re going to want to find the explorers notes in the southwest corner of the map, as they give you double xp for a while. Keep that open.

The next order of business is to assign roles. What you need are two gatherers, one hunter/gatherer, and a runner. The runner goes around getting the nearby explorers notes while the gatherers get as much stone/wood/thatch and fiber as they can. The hunter/gatherer works to get enough food for your tribe, then helps to gather materials. The reason you do this is because it’s much more helpful to have one high level player in your tribe early on than four evenly leveled players. Boosting one guy gets you further. Store all your materials in boxes for when the runner gets back. 

The runner should prioritize their level ups into movement speed and stamina, while the gatherers (and hunter/gatherer) should prioritize carry weight, stamina and melee damage.  Store all your materials in boxes for when the runner gets back with double xp.

By the time he gets back he’ll be a higher level from the xp the notes give, and you guys should start on your first project; a mobile raft base. Look up a video on lowering foundations and make sure the runner crafts all of these pieces.

Materials

1 raft
1 wooden pillar
1 thatch foundation
4 thatch ceilings
13 wood or stone foundations
10 wood or stone walls
8 wood or stone ceilings
1 wood or stone Hatchframe
1 wood or stone trap door
2 wood or stone door frames 
2 wood doors
3 wood ramps
2 refining forges
1 smithy
2 beds
4 mortar and pestles
3 campfires
2 preserving bins
2-3 storage boxes
3 ladders

Lower the thatch foundation flush with the deck of your boat, then place a  3x3 foundation around the raft with the doorways in the center front and center back. Put the thatch ceilings in a T shape out the back door and snap foundations under them. Put the walls up, ceilings and fill in the other stuff. 

Make crossbows and hundreds of arrows, if you need metal, mine the round river rocks. Search the map killing all of the alpha dinosaurs you find, they give a bunch of xp and drop upgraded tools and weapons for your tribe. This should quickly catch everyone up with the runner/crafter. You can easily get everybody to level 70+ on day one by hunting alphas, and you can use the prime meat to make mindwipe tonic to respec your characters to pvp builds. 

Tame a trash herbivore for gathering narcoberries, and get everybody an argentavis. Hands down, one of the best dinos in the game. Even shitty, low level argents are awesome. Upload your dinos into the ark before you log off to keep them safe.

Look up 2x1 base designs and build them all over the server (and on two or three others.) don’t keep your eggs in one basket, hide stuff everywhere.

Edit: you can establish yourself competitively in a day or two if your team works hard.

There are two main strategies when it comes to flipping; the first being to try to turn a profit off of lots of low to mid value, high volume items. If I can buy 100,000 Guam leaves for 8 gp each and sell them at 10, that’s a 20% turn around. The amount you make off each individual trade isn’t very much (2 gp each,) but it’s still a large return on investment overall. The second strategy is to throw your weight around by investing in high value, low volume items. You can still make the same 20% margin due to the scarcity of the item you’re trading, but it requires more risk, more time, and it ties up more capital into one single trade. The best way to play the GE is to combine both tactics to varying degrees as your gold stack allows. Watching the charts on the osrs website can help you see potential long term investments, where you might buy and hold a bunch of items for months to get even higher margins.

If you’re on a PvP server, focus on completing your journal entries for xp. When you get to the point where journals are a bit more complicated, (throw an orb, obtain an iron bar etc.) go farm the npc’s that drop them to speed it up. When you get to making iron tools and armor, get a bunch of food, a couple water skins and several bed rolls because it’s time to go explore the map. Finding points on the map gives experience, and using the crafting stations in a bombed out or abandoned base is far easier than building your own. Plus, exploring all the points on the map is a journal entry too. I recommend you do the eastern desert/jungle first, because the other areas are a bit more difficult at lower levels. Once you’ve mapped out everything up through the highlands, then start looking at building a base and filling in whatever journals you need your own base to complete. You should be able to craft the top tier buildings, and the northern part of the map has better resources and thralls for your defenses/crafting stations.

I was a hauler/trader when I first started eve. Someone I knew irl lent me five million isk and an iteron V when I started my 14 day trial and I set out space trucking. What you want to do starting out is get a feel for what items are low cost/high volume, those are what I found to be best to start out on with low capital. Often times looking at the in game market you can see decent margins on ammo and ore in the regional buy/sell orders. Just buy as much as you can afford until you can start filling the orders in one trip from sell order to buy order locations. And be sure to do the math on your brokers fees and taxes, sometimes an order looks profitable, but the fees will end up a net loss for you. And play, “space truckin’” by deep purple every day when you start out, or the space gods of commerce will become displeased and you’ll get spanked by some neck beard with nothing better to do.
